title: IBBI Disciplinary Committee Issues & Standards Analysis
text:
__Issue Analysis — IBBI Disciplinary Committee Order \(Anonymised\)__

*CIRP of a stalled group\-housing Corporate Debtor — conduct of the Resolution Professional\. Five alleged contraventions: three upheld, two dropped\.*

__\#__

__Allegation \(with provisions\)__

__Stand of Mr\. X \(RP\)__

__Decision of IBBI__

__I__

Executed construction contract and issued work order __without valid Authority / RERA approvals__; failed to inform allottees of the implications\.

*S\.17\(2\)\(e\) r/w 23\(2\); 208\(2\)\(a\)&\(e\); Reg\.7\(2\)\(a\)&\(h\); Clauses 1 & 14\.*

Work was only __interior finishing__ — exempt under RERA s\.3\(2\)\(c\) and Authority Building Reg\.5\(5\)\(e\); no marketing or sale; sealing order quashed by the High Court; in\-principle approval obtained; CoC kept informed\.

__Held — contravention upheld\. __Contract scope in fact covered __civil / structural construction of 7 towers “in all respects,”__ not mere internal alterations; activities also __violated the High Court order dated 03\.12\.2024__\. Submissions found not tenable\.

__II__

__Deviated from BBA terms__ — excluded liveability items \(lifts, DG, STP, boundary wall, etc\.\); levied ₹150/sq\.ft\. interim finance and ₹25,000 token not provided for in the BBAs\.

*S\.208\(2\)\(a\)&\(e\); Reg\.7\(2\)\(a\)&\(h\); Clauses 1 & 14\.*

Scope was CoC\-approved interior finishing; exclusions deliberated across the 38th–40th / 43rd CoC; lifts/DG/STP procured separately to cut cost; ₹150/sq\.ft\. approved u/s 25\(2\)\(c\) to bridge the __GST gap \(12% vs 18%\)__, to be raised only at __85% participation__ \(none raised yet\); token set off against demand\. Relied on Shailesh Verma\.

__Not held — accepted\. __In insolvency, funds are inadequate; stakeholders legitimately __prioritised works within available funds by substantial vote__, and such funding fits the Code’s interim\-finance scheme\. Submission accepted\.

__III__

__Material non\-disclosures in the IM__ — land area, units pending / completed, Authority & RERA non\-approvals, lift/DG/STP budget treatment, unsold inventory\.

*S\.208\(2\)\(a\)&\(e\); Reg\.36\(2\)\(a\); Reg\.7\(2\)\(a\)&\(h\); Clause 14\.*

All items disclosed across IM / VDR / annexures — land area \(p\.33\), units \(pp\.34–37\), Authority & RERA position \(p\.25 \+ writ copies shared\), exclusions \(p\.29\)\.

__Not held — save scrap\. __DC satisfied that __Reg\.36\(2\) disclosures were substantially complied with__, even if spread across IM, annexures and VDR\. Sole exception — site materials / scrap — carried over to Contravention IV\.

__IV__

__Failed to disclose site materials__ in the IM and to the CoC; failed to report sale proceeds\.

*S\.25\(1\); 208\(2\)\(a\)&\(e\); Reg\.7\(2\)\(a\)&\(h\); Clause 14\.*

Inventory disclosed; scrap was construction waste __already charged off__ in prior years; sale done with CoC approval \(30th / 33rd CoC\), via e\-bidding to highest bidder; report shared with homebuyers; proceeds \(₹28,43,325 from 52\.745 MT\) discussed in 39th CoC\. Relied on Reg\.29 and JAMEWA\.

__Held — partly\. __Sale process and proceeds disclosure were in order, but the materials — __known to Mr\. X since the 26th CoC \(10\.10\.2022\)__ — were __omitted from the updated IM \(07\.02\.2023\)__\. The “charged\-off” defence was rejected; disclosure was his duty\. Contravention held on the non\-disclosure limb\.

__V__

__Issued work order to the Contractor Consortium while the RA Consortium’s plan \(common members\) was near submission__, conferring an unfair edge / influencing CoC voting\.

*S\.208\(2\)\(a\)&\(e\); Reg\.7\(2\)\(a\)&\(h\); Clauses 1, 3 & 14\.*

Award and plan approval fell within __CoC commercial wisdom__; contract award \(e\-voting closed 07\.12\.2023\) __preceded the 2nd Form G__ \(01\.02\.2024\); work order was procedural, on 60% tower\-wise homebuyer consent; Clause 48 let the CoC abandon/reduce; __no legal bar__ on awarding a contract to an RA before plan approval\. Relied on K\. Sashidhar\.

__Split, then upheld\. J\. Prasad \(WTM\): __conduct not bonafide; vitiated transparency; conflict undisclosed → __3\-yr suspension\.__

__S\. Garg \(WTM\): __award already CoC\-known, so execution could not sway the CoC; flagged for re\-investigation the PRAGATI withdrawal without EMD forfeiture, the EMD furnished by cheque instead of Demand Draft as required by the RFRP \(and whether that non\-conforming plan should have been placed before the CoC at all\), and the Clause 48 structuring → __2\-yr suspension\.__

__3rd DC \(05\.05\.2026\): __Mr\. X __admitted he never disclosed the conflict__ despite great commonality; as RP / CoC\-Chairman he bore a non\-delegable duty of full, fair and timely disclosure and could not shelter behind commercial wisdom absent complete disclosure\. __Upheld; concurred with J\. Prasad\.__

## __Net outcome__

Of five contraventions, __three were upheld__ \(I, IV – disclosure limb, V\) and __two dropped__ \(II, III\)\. On the split point \(V\), the third DC concurred with the harsher view\. __Registration suspended for 3 years__, effective 30 days from 05\.05\.2026\. A related thread — withdrawal of the earlier plan without EMD forfeiture, the EMD tendered by cheque rather than Demand Draft as required by the RFRP, and the Clause 48 structuring — was left open for separate investigation\.

__Thread running through the upheld counts: __*reliance on CoC commercial wisdom is a valid shield only where the RP has first placed complete, contemporaneous material — especially conflicts of interest — before a fully\-informed CoC\.*

## __Anonymisation key__

- __Mr\. X = __the Insolvency Professional / Resolution Professional \(RP\)
- __CD = __Corporate Debtor \(a stalled group\-housing developer\)
- __Authority / RERA = __the land\-leasing Development Authority; the real\-estate regulator
- __Contractor Consortium = __consortium awarded the “Pool & Build” construction contract
- __RA Consortium = __resolution\-applicant consortium sharing a common member / director with the Contractor Consortium
